title: assistant-onboard Skill Behavior Eval Fixtures
description: Provider-neutral offline eval cases for the assistant-onboard skill's systematic codebase learning workflow.

activation_cases.user_request: Map this project before changing it.
Make a small change in this familiar codebase.

recommended_use: Run each case with the assistant-onboard skill instructions loaded.
Compare the local response against scoped mapping, source evidence, relevant observations, gap handling, and persistence authorization.
Use deterministic substring checks as offline proxies for contract adherence, not semantic grading.

cases.title: New repo onboarding produces orientation
cases.purpose: Checks that a new repository onboarding request performs surface scan, architecture mapping, pattern recognition, and orientation output.
cases.prompt: Get familiar with this repo before we start changing anything.
setup_context: The assistant-onboard skill instructions are active.
The current project has not been onboarded in this session.
The surface scan classifies the repository as medium.
No focus_area or depth was specified.
expected_behavior: Infers the current project and an appropriate scope from context.
Reads project instructions, README, build manifests, and relevant CI before tracing representative paths.
Builds a scoped map from local evidence, including entry points, commands, conventions, relevant risks, and coverage gaps.
Reports ownership, lifecycle, type, or design-pressure observations only when inspected evidence makes them relevant.
Samples representative source and tests rather than claiming to read every file.
Returns orientation in the conversation without unauthorized persistence or production edits.
pass_criteria: Key paths have concrete roles and conventions have source examples.
Build/test/run commands are source-backed where discoverable.
Relevant risks and specific gaps are reported.
Project size does not force empty architecture arrays, phase transcripts, or a status envelope.
fail_signals: Starts editing project files before onboarding.
Claims to read every file as the default approach.
Asks generic questions that are not tied to discovered gaps.

cases.title: Medium onboarding omits irrelevant architecture arrays
cases.purpose: Checks that repository size does not create architecture ceremony when inspected evidence has no relevant candidates.
cases.prompt: Onboard this medium repository and return the orientation.
setup_context: The assistant-onboard skill instructions are active.
The surface scan classifies the repository as medium.
Architecture inspection found no semantic-type or design-pressure candidates.
expected_behavior: Returns a useful scoped map after inspection.
Omits irrelevant semantic-type and design-pressure candidate arrays.
Reports coverage limits without inventing redesign work.
pass_criteria: The orientation describes entry points, commands, and conventions.
No candidate arrays are required solely because of project size.
fail_signals: Invents a redesign to fill candidate arrays.

cases.title: Small onboarding may omit architecture candidates
cases.purpose: Checks that small onboarding remains proportionate.
cases.prompt: Onboard this small repository and return the orientation.
setup_context: The assistant-onboard skill instructions are active.
The surface scan classifies the repository as small.
expected_behavior: Returns a concise scoped map of the small project.
Omits irrelevant architecture candidate arrays.
pass_criteria: The response keeps the orientation proportional to a small project.
fail_signals: Requires architecture candidate arrays solely because the project is small.

cases.title: Incremental onboarding refreshes context
cases.purpose: Checks that returning to a known project reads existing orientation, checks recent changes, updates rather than overwrites, and reports specific unknowns.
cases.prompt: Refresh your project context; this repo changed since our last session.
setup_context: The assistant-onboard skill instructions are active.
A project-local orientation artifact already exists.
The user asks for an incremental refresh rather than first-time onboarding.
expected_behavior: Reads the existing orientation when policy allows.
Checks relevant source and git history against the recorded refresh basis.
Reports stable changes and specific gaps.
Preserves existing notes and writes only when persistence is authorized; otherwise returns refreshed context in conversation.
pass_criteria: Uses the existing orientation and recent changes as evidence.
Preserves user notes and does not infer write authorization merely from a refresh request.
fail_signals: Regenerates the orientation from scratch without reading the existing artifact.
Overwrites memory without preserving existing sections.
Reports no unknowns without inspecting changed areas.

cases.title: Size inventory uses local tools and stays an orientation fact
cases.purpose: Checks that a size or language inventory uses git-tracked files and counters already on PATH, excludes dependency and generated directories, and treats counts as orientation facts rather than quality.
cases.prompt: How big is this repository and which languages does it use? Give me line counts per language.
setup_context: The assistant-onboard skill instructions are active.
The repository is a Git checkout with node_modules/, dist/ and vendor/ directories.
No code counter such as scc, tokei or cloc is installed on PATH.
The user has not authorized installing tools.
expected_behavior: Enumerates files with git ls-files so ignored files are excluded.
Excludes dependency, build, vendored and generated directories explicitly.
Falls back to grouping git ls-files output by extension because no counter is on PATH, and installs nothing.
Reports Markdown and instruction files separately from code.
States that the counts are orientation facts, not a quality judgement.
pass_criteria: Installs nothing and asks before any installation.
Separates documentation or instruction files from code.
Does not present size as quality.
fail_signals: Recommends installing a package, including with --break-system-packages.
Treats a file or line count as a quality judgement.
Counts node_modules, dist or vendor content as project code.
Claims full coverage from a sample.

forbidden_substrings: higher quality because it has more lines
